$comment: What bootstrap-nest.mjs installs into ~/.buzz, and how.
mode     — file permissions. Executables get 0755; nothing here is secret, so
there is no 0600 entry. The .secrets/ directory itself is created
0700 by the bootstrap and never populated from this repo.
Directories are 0700 across the board. Nothing in ~/.buzz is read by
another user or another process — one Mac, one operator — and several
of these accumulate client-adjacent material as the agents work:
WORK_LOGS and OUTBOX by definition, RESEARCH and .scratch in practice,
.claude/agents/ the project and dataset ids. These were 0755, which
made a research workspace world-readable from the first bootstrap for
no benefit anybody could name.
resolve  — whether {{TOKEN}} markers are replaced with local-values.json values
on the way in. See $resolveComment below; this is not a blanket yes.
ifAbsent — install only when the target does not exist. For files an operator is
expected to edit: overwriting on the next `git pull` + bootstrap would
silently discard their changes. A differing file is reported, not
replaced. Everything without this flag is ours and is kept in sync.
Deliberately NOT in this manifest:
Stu's app              buzz-agents/agents/stu/app is source, not configuration.
bin/stu reads it out of the checkout: bootstrap resolves
{{STU_APP}} to that absolute path on the way in. Copying it
would fork the tree the moment someone edited the copy, and
the first run builds web/dist inside it. Move the clone and
re-run bootstrap; STU_APP in the environment overrides.
bin/toolbox            154 MB. Fetched from upstream by version + checksum.
mcp/bq-<slug>.yaml     Generated per channel by deploy-claire-channel.sh from
mcp/templates/. Versioning rendered output invites edits
to the copy instead of the template.
.claude/agents/*-<slug>.md  Same — rendered from mcp/templates/agents/. The three
agents/*.md without a slug ARE in this manifest: Barb and her
two checkers are identical for every operator, so there is
nothing to render. They use fromRoot — see that entry.
drive-fence/diag-export.mjs  A one-off investigation into a Drive 403, not runtime.
.secrets/*             Service-account keys. Never versioned, never templated.
.claude/skills/buzz-cli/  Ships with Buzz Desktop; not ours to install or update.
$resolveComment: Token resolution is per file, because 'resolve everything' is wrong twice.
RESEARCH_CHANNEL_DATASET_SCHEMA.md is resolve:false on purpose. It is the DDL
source of truth, and deploy-claire-channel.sh substitutes {{BQ_PROJECT}} itself
at deploy time (its sed also handles the per-channel @dataset). Baking the project
in at bootstrap would mean a later `deploy --project other-project` silently emits
DDL naming the project chosen at install time instead.
The trap that follows: deploy-claire-channel.sh is itself resolve:true, so a token
written literally in its sed pattern gets resolved along with everything else, and
the pattern turns into the install-time project id. It then matches nothing in the
unresolved guide, the substitution is a silent no-op, and BigQuery rejects the DDL
for an invalid project id named after the token. The script assembles that pattern
at runtime instead. Do not 'simplify' it back to a literal.
JANICE_REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md is resolve:true and must stay that way. Janice reads it
at runtime for the channel routing table. An unresolved {{JANICE_CHANNEL}} there is
not a cosmetic problem — she would post findings to a channel named after the token.

$comment: Self-service. The reference binary is 1.8.0
(`toolbox version 1.8.0+binary.darwin.arm64.44d1a05`) and it downloads from
Google's official release bucket, checksum-verified against the pin above.
Earlier revisions of this file recorded 1.8.0 as unfetchable. That was a
dead-bucket error, not a publishing gap: the upstream project was RENAMED
from `genai-toolbox` to `googleapis/mcp-toolbox`, and its release bucket
moved with it. The old `storage.googleapis.com/genai-toolbox` bucket was
frozen at v1.1.0 at the point of the rename, which is why every later
version 404s there while v1.0.0 still returns 200. The live bucket is
`mcp-toolbox-for-databases`, per the install instructions in the upstream
README at tag v1.8.0.
Verified 2026-08-04: the darwin/arm64 download from the URL above is
BYTE-IDENTICAL to the vetted binary on the machine this stack was built on —
same 153,986,752 bytes, same sha256 c69e0b5e…, and the recorded checksum was
taken from that vetted binary, not from the download. So the pin below is a
genuine cross-check of provenance, not a self-referential hash of whatever
the bucket happened to serve.
A checksum mismatch fails closed and refuses to install: this is the
component that enforces the `allowedDatasets` fence, so a wrong or tampered
binary must never half-work.
Only darwin/arm64 is recorded, because that is the only platform this stack runs
on: buzz and buzz-acp ship exclusively as arm64 Mach-O inside Buzz.app.
Re-pin with: shasum -a 256 ~/.buzz/bin/toolbox
To move to a newer toolbox, bump referenceVersion and add the matching
checksum — download it, run it, confirm the dataset fence still holds with
bin/verify-channel-isolation.py, and only then record the hash.
The pass reader Analyst and Persona both use: survey a conversation from its tags,
serve line ranges and record which were served, and check that a cited quote actually
appears in the line it cites.
That last one is the reason it exists. Both definitions warned in almost the same words
that a quote recalled from a window you no longer hold reads right and does not match the
line, and that the write path verifies the line_id exists but never the quote. So the one
mistake both prompts named was the one nothing caught.
It lives in bin/ rather than beside a skill because two subagents own it. A tool sits next
to its skill when it has one owner; copying this into both would be the divergence the
shared BigQuery helper was extracted to avoid.
Shared BigQuery access for the agent tools: run a statement, escape a string literal,
name a table. Extracted rather than copied when the tagger tool needed the same three
things — a second hand-written copy of SQL-literal escaping is a divergence waiting to
become a broken write in one agent and not the other.
Both tools import it through BUZZ_HOME rather than a relative path, because they live
under agents/ in the repo and only meet this file once installed.
The batch server Tagger drives. Unlike the ingest tool it does NOT replace the model —
which tags a line earns is judgement. It owns everything around that: the batch cursor,
validating each tag against the active library and that tag's own threshold, the MERGE,
the accounting, and the coverage proof.
The coverage proof is why it exists. Untagged lines and never-read lines are
indistinguishable in the tags table, which is how the previous pipeline's LIMIT 500 went
unnoticed against longer transcripts. The cursor is derived from batch rows recorded in
ingest_runs, so it survives a crash and cannot be misremembered.
fromRoot and resolve:true for the same reasons as the ingest tool below.
The transcript ingest Scribe runs instead of walking the document herself. It lives
under agents/claire/subagents/scribe/ rather than in nest/bin/ because it is the
subagent's tool: the prompt that invokes it and the script it invokes version together,
and a change to one that forgets the other is the failure worth designing out. That is
the Claude skill layout — a SKILL.md beside the resources it uses.
fromRoot for the same reason Barb's agents use it: the source is under agents/, not
under nest/. Unlike those, resolve:true — it carries {{BQ_PROJECT}} as the default
project, exactly like sync-tag-dictionary.mjs above.
It is NOT a build output, so there is no `npm run agents:build` step behind it.
build-agents.mjs reads only SKILL.md out of a subagent directory and ignores the rest,
which is what lets the tool sit beside its own documentation without being rendered.
The credential guard, and the command-reading helpers both it and the stale-checkout
guard use. Registered in .claude/settings.json with NO `if` key, unlike its siblings:
on the day it was written Bash(git *) fired with git not leading and Bash(curl *) did
not fire with curl leading, unexplained by anyone. A guardrail behind a mechanism
nobody can explain is not a guardrail. The command test lives in the script, where
guard-credential-store.test.mjs asserts it in both directions.
Barb and her two checkers, installed for every operator rather than rendered per
client. A subagent is reachable only if its file sits in .claude/agents/, and these
three are the same for everybody: a design reviewer touches no dataset, no Drive
folder and no channel, so there is nothing to render and nothing to fence.
All three or none. Barb without checker and feisty still runs, and what she does
instead is skim — the skills corpus is ~220k tokens and the fan-out is how it gets
read rather than sampled. A partial install fails silently and looks like a clean
review.
fromRoot because these are build outputs of scripts/build-agents.mjs, whose source is
agents/barb/. Run `npm run agents:build` before bootstrapping if they are missing.
resolve:false — they carry no {{TOKEN}}. Barb is told where the checkout is by
whoever dispatches her, which is what lets the same file serve a Buzz agent and a
plain session.

$settingsComment: .claude/settings.json is load-bearing for two of the four agents, and was missing
from this manifest until 2026-08-04 — so every operator but the first would have got
a Janice who never reviewed anything and never said why.
hooks.Stop      runs bin/wake-janice.sh after every turn. This is the ONLY thing
that triggers a Janice review. Without it she is installed,
healthy, and permanently idle — and silence is also what a clean
review looks like, so the failure is invisible.
hooks.PreToolUse  guard-published-text.mjs on git/gh/buzz/curl, and
guard-commit-trailers.mjs on git — the latter denies a commit that
would land without the operator's Signed-off-by and Co-authored-by.
AGENTS.md had required both for months and they were missed twice in
two days, so the rule lives here rather than in four prompts.
guard-stale-checkout.mjs on Bash/Read/Grep/Glob denies reading source
from a REPOS/ directory with no .git — a leftover copy nothing runs.
Two agents cited one as the live app in a week, the second after its
own tool printed 'fatal: not a git repository'. Prose could not fix
it: AGENTS.md is read at session start and sessions are pooled, so a
rule added today misses every session already running. Settings are
consulted per tool call. Listing, diffing, moving and removing such a
directory stay allowed — that is how it gets cleaned up.
permissions     allow: [Agent] — Claire fans out parallel Scribe/Tagger subagents.
MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS  60000. BigQuery result sets truncate at the default.
resolve:true for {{BUZZ_HOME}} — the hook needs an absolute path, and the nest is
not always ~/.buzz (--nest, $BUZZ_HOME). bootstrap-nest.mjs derives this value from
the target directory rather than asking for it; it is not in local-values.json.
ifAbsent:true because this is an operator's own settings file. They may add hooks or
permissions of their own, and a later bootstrap must not throw those away. The cost
is that changes we make here do not reach an existing nest automatically — bootstrap
says so, with a diff hint, rather than deciding for them.

prerequisites.name: Buzz Desktop
prerequisites.why: Supplies both the buzz CLI and buzz-acp. Neither is distributed separately, and both are arm64 macOS only.

prerequisites.name: claude CLI
prerequisites.why: The runtime every agent is configured against (runtime: claude).

prerequisites.name: node
prerequisites.why: Runs the drive-fence MCP server, the tag-dictionary sync, and this bootstrap.

prerequisites.name: gcloud
prerequisites.why: Only needed to create a new client dataset and service account via setup_gcp.sh.
prerequisites.fix: Install the Google Cloud SDK if you will be onboarding a new client.
